_title: 5 Blogs Worth Reading Before You Travel Europe by Train — WoW Train · glosx.app
_desc: Five independent blogs that make train travel in Europe easier: practical guides, route ideas and slow-travel stories, chosen by the WoW Train team.
b1: 5 Blogs Worth Reading Before You Travel Europe by Train
b2: By WoW Train · November 2026 · 6 min read
b3: We read a lot of travel blogs while we build WoW Train. These five are the ones we keep going back to when a reader asks how to cross Europe by rail. Each one does something different, and each one is worth your time.
b5: One of the clearest starting points for anyone planning Europe on a budget. Their complete guide to train travel walks through tickets, passes and booking step by step, without jargon.
b6: Read: Complete guide to train travel in Europe
b7: 2. Show Me The Journey
b8: A site built entirely around rail: train information by country, journey pages and station guides. When you want to know how a specific line works, it is a great place to look.
b11: Stories and routes from people who love trains, with a strong eye for the journey itself. A good read when you are choosing which line to ride, not only where to go.
b14: Slow travel done well, with detailed, practical posts. Their guide to getting from Lisbon to Sintra by train is a model of how to explain a short trip clearly.
b15: Read: How to get from Lisbon to Sintra by train
b17: In-depth city guides that pay attention to how you actually get around on the ground. Their Europe section is full of ideas for linking cities without flying.
b19: Planning one of these trips? Our route guides cover Lisbon → Porto, Paris → Amsterdam and Vienna → Salzburg, with times from official open data.
b20: Writing about one of these routes? Take our times with you
b21: Every route page on WoW Train has a block called “Add this route to your blog”: a small card with the route summary and, where we have the official timetable, first train, last train and trains per day. Enter your blog and your name, and you get a short code that shows the card in WordPress, Ghost or any editor, with times that update by themselves. It is free. Try it on Paris → Amsterdam or Tokyo → Kyoto, or find your route in the route index.
b22: Plan the whole route in one go.
b23: Describe your trip and WoW Train suggests the trains for every leg, with booking links.
